goal: Deliver one consumer-only Pafio sync loop that deterministically locks, verifies and materializes dependencies, then emits the minimal Styio resolution-v1 contract.
description: Scope: Closure: capability - one manifest-to-resolution sync transaction for path and registry dependency graphs; own the current manifest/lock/resolver/registry/security/store path, add the minimal resolution-v1 contract and focused tests, and do not extend compiler, toolchain, cloud, IDE, hosted-control-plane, Git-source, vendor, pack, or publish behavior. Context: the repository already contains a working exact-version resolver and completed supply-chain hardening, but its CLI and plan mix package consumption with compiler workflow, tool installation, cloud policy, registry service operation, and Vityo aggregation. Target: sync prepares an immutable graph, reuses a valid lock, materializes missing SHA-256 objects through bounded single-flight work, commits lock and then resolution-v1 as ordered atomic files, and reproduces the same state with --locked --offline. Design Considerations: retain O(V + E) exact-version traversal for this closure; use hash maps only for lookup, sorted vectors for graph/output determinism, per-digest locks plus temp/hash/prescan/rename for CAS commits, and a project-local resolution file modeled as a narrow package-id-to-root map. Mutable path/workspace packages expose a null content digest rather than a false manifest-derived digest. Design Value: creates the smallest independently useful and trustworthy package-manager kernel and a stable handoff that lets later ownership migrations delete broad Pafio surfaces. Constraints & Risks: preserve completed TUF/archive/atomic-write protections; no absolute paths in lockfiles; resolution commits last and digest mismatch rejects an interrupted cross-file commit; no full regression during implementation; naming migration and range solving are separate future capabilities with no compatibility shims.

symbols.name: SerializeResolutionCanonical
symbols.signature: std::string SerializeResolutionCanonical(const ResolvedGraphResult &, std::string_view manifest_sha256, std::string_view lock_sha256)

interfaces.name: sync transaction
interfaces.inputs: validated manifest, optional lock, resolve flags and registry/cache state
interfaces.outputs: verified CAS objects plus canonical lock and resolution-v1 committed as ordered atomic files
errors: registry trust or content verification failure
bounded lock wait or atomic commit failure

interfaces.name: resolution-v1
interfaces.inputs: immutable resolved graph plus manifest and lock digests
interfaces.outputs: canonical project-local JSON package-id-to-source-root mapping with registry SHA-256 and null mutable-local digest
errors: duplicate package id or dangling dependency alias

dependencies.reason: Registry metadata must be verified before it can enter resolution or the content-addressed store.
The sync transaction commits each file atomically in lock-then-resolution order so digest mismatch rejects an interrupted cross-file commit.
The black-box Styio handoff fixture validates the exact published resolution contract.

decisions.composition: one prepare/commit sync transaction with the resolution file committed last
decisions.algorithms: lock-first exact-version DFS with active-stack cycle detection; O(V + E)
decisions.data_structures: unordered lookup maps, compact node vectors, sorted dependency vectors and a unique digest work set
decisions.state: portable lock is committed state; SHA-256 CAS is immutable shared state; resolution-v1 is generated machine-local state and uses null content_sha256 for mutable path/workspace packages
decisions.isolation: the core dependency graph excludes compiler workflow, toolchain, cloud, IDE and hosted control-plane modules
decisions.concurrency: bounded workers across distinct digests and single-flight plus per-digest file locks for identical content

test_seams: failure injection before each atomic commit

acceptance_criteria.text: A mixed path-plus-registry transitive graph completes one sync and emits a lock and resolution-v1 whose bytes are identical on an unchanged second run.
After a warm sync, --locked --offline performs no network access or extraction and resolves every package root from verified local state.

Corrupt artifacts, traversal archives, interrupted ordered commits and two-process same-digest races either recover online or fail closed offline; no torn individual file/CAS object or resolution accepted against incomplete state is observable.
The resolution-v1 schema and minimal Styio consumer accept the canonical fixture and reject stale digests, duplicate IDs, dangling aliases, missing roots and unknown schema versions.
Source/target dependency evidence proves the thin core and resolution schema do not depend on or expose compiler workflow, toolchain, cloud, IDE or hosted-control-plane behavior.
